summary.text: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than a proton's.
Neutrons sit in atomic nuclei with a similar number of protons, and atoms of an element that differ only in neutron number are isotopes.
A free neutron decays into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino with a mean lifetime of about 15 minutes, and neutrons are essential to nuclear power.

facts.label: Free neutron lifetime
facts.value: Mean of about 15 minutes before decay

facts.label: Nobel Prize
facts.value: Chadwick won the 1935 Physics prize for it

items.prompt: Two atoms are the same element, but one has more neutrons. How are they related?

options.label: They are ions of the same element
They are isotopes of the same element
They are two different elements
They are the same atom at different energies

items.explain: Atoms of a chemical element that differ only in neutron number are called isotopes.

items.prompt: Early researchers saw a penetrating radiation unbent by an electric field and took it for gamma rays. What did Chadwick show it really was?

options.label: Fast protons slowed by paraffin
Light waves with an unusually short wavelength
Uncharged particles of roughly the same mass as a proton
Electrons with the charge screened away

items.explain: His experiments showed the radiation was made of uncharged particles with about the same mass as the proton.

items.prompt: By the late 1920s, physicists doubted the nucleus was made of protons plus nuclear electrons. What was the problem?

options.label: Quantum theory said a confined electron would hold too much energy
Electrons are far too heavy to fit in a nucleus
Electrons would cancel the protons' charge entirely
Nuclei were found to contain no charge at all

items.explain: An electron confined to a nucleus would have more energy than the binding energy and would escape.

items.prompt: Where are free neutrons produced in large numbers?

options.label: In ordinary chemical burning
In static electricity discharges
In the heating of metals
In nuclear fission and fusion

items.explain: Free neutrons are produced copiously in nuclear fission and fusion.

items.prompt: Researchers bombarded uranium with neutrons in 1938. What did they find happened to the nuclei?

options.label: They swallowed the neutrons and grew heavier
They broke into lighter elements
They released protons and turned to gold
They stayed whole but became radioactive

items.explain: Hahn, Meitner and Strassmann found the uranium nuclei fractionated into lighter elements.

items.prompt: A free neutron is left alone. What eventually happens to it?

options.label: It decays into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino
It stays unchanged forever
It splits into two lighter neutrons
It merges with the nearest atom's electron

items.explain: A free neutron spontaneously decays, with a mean lifetime of about 15 minutes.
